module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 551

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/551](https://www.erdosproblems.com/551)
- [BoEr73] Bondy, J. A. and Erdős, P., Ramsey numbers for cycles in graphs. J. Combin. Theory
  Ser. B (1973), 46-54.
- [Ni05] Nikiforov, V., The cycle-complete graph Ramsey numbers. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2005),
  349-370.
- [KLS21] Keevash, P., Long, E. and Skokan, J., Cycle-complete Ramsey numbers.
  Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2021), 277-302.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos551

/--
Prove that
$$R(C_k,K_n)=(k-1)(n-1)+1$$
for $k\geq n\geq 3$ (except when $n=k=3$).

Asked by Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp.
This problem is #18 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_551 :
    ∀ (k n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → n ≤ k → ¬(n = 3 ∧ k = 3) →
      SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph k)
        (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) = (k - 1) * (n - 1) + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
For sufficiently large $n$ and every $k\geq n$, $R(C_k,K_n)=(k-1)(n-1)+1$.

Keevash, Long, and Skokan [KLS21] have proved this identity when
$k\geq C\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}$ for some constant $C$, thus establishing the conjecture
for sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_551.variants.sufficiently_large :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ k : ℕ, n ≤ k →
      SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph k)
        (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n)) = (k - 1) * (n - 1) + 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos551

sources_consulted: Keevash, Long and Skokan, Cycle-complete Ramsey numbers, Introduction and Theorem 1.1; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1807.06376
Nikiforov, The Cycle-Complete graph Ramsey numbers, Introduction, main theorem and concluding remarks; LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0404501
Bondy and Erdős, Ramsey numbers for cycles in graphs (1973), especially the definition of Ramsey numbers and Theorems 4–5: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-22.pdf
Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp, On cycle-complete graph Ramsey numbers (1978), Introduction and concluding questions: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1978-18.pdf
Independent Erdős problem database, overview and entry 551: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md
review.notes:
Both declarations faithfully state the cited mathematics. The sufficiently-large variant is a valid corollary of KLS21 Theorem 1.1. Its eventual quantifier supplies one threshold uniform over all k ≥ n, so omitting explicit small-n exclusions is harmless. Inspection of graphRamsey and its dependencies confirmed ordinary non-induced Ramsey containment; finite Ramsey theory ensures its defining set is nonempty. Scratch Lean checks verified cycle adjacency, boundary containment examples, safe natural subtraction, and equivalence with an explicit eventual threshold.

Direct access to erdosproblems.com/551 was blocked by Cloudflare, so its current official status could not be read. Mathematical faithfulness was verified from the primary papers instead. The independent Erdős database records #551 as 'decidable', explicitly meaning still unsolved, consistent with 'research open'; KLS21 supports the solved tag on the variant.
